statusText: CME equity-index futures have been shut since Friday's 21:00 UTC weekly close and do not reopen until roughly 22:00 UTC on Sunday 16 August, so there is no observable NQ price path this hour and none anywhere in the 24-hour horizon, which ends at 04:00 UTC on 16 August - still about 18 hours before the reopen. Tail is 9% (low), holding the action at EA_ON and the status green: pathological one-way structure cannot form while no venue is quoting, and the low non-zero level prices weekend headline discontinuity rather than any observed extension. The last confirmed structure, re-verified this hour from primary sources, supports that reading - NQ futures settled at 30,148.25, down 40.25 points or 0.13%, mid-range inside a 30,028.50-30,283.00 band, while the Nasdaq-100 cash index closed at 30,046.14 (-0.13%) about 2.3% below its 52-week high of 30,762.20, with VIX at 14.25 (-2.60%) and the latest H.15 showing 2Y 4.15%, 10Y 4.63% and 30Y 5.21%. Stress is deliberately held at 45% (elevated) rather than decayed, because nothing resolved overnight: the Strait of Hormuz is still shut with fewer than ten vessels a day transiting, the U.S. naval blockade is still in force and Tehran still conditions any reopening on it ending, WTI sits at $82.40 and Brent at $88.52 after a weekly gain of about 5%, and Friday's U.S. consumer data was sharply soft with Retail Sales -0.6% against +0.1% expected and Michigan sentiment 51.0 against 54.5. Confidence is 59% (medium-low): everything except the price path is fresh and primary-sourced, but the price path is the input that matters most and it does not exist this hour. recommendation: Action is EA_ON with a green status, derived from current Tail (9%) alone. No venue is quoting NQ anywhere in the 24-hour horizon and no scheduled U.S. macro release falls inside it, so there is no basis for a directional or event-driven block in this window; existing-position management, exits and emergency protection remain active as always. The operative checkpoint is the CME reopen near 22:00 UTC on Sunday 16 August, where a full weekend of accumulated headlines would express as an opening gap rather than as intraday structure - the danger window brackets that reopen and its first 90 minutes of price discovery. Gap risk is genuinely two-way: Iran and Oman have settled the route coordinates and Tehran calls a deal very close, yet Iran ties any reopening to the end of the U.S. naval blockade plus broader concessions, while Washington signals an indefinite blockade and tells Americans to expect higher pump prices. Either thread can move crude before equities can price it, and Friday's weak consumer prints leave a second, unrelated growth-scare channel open into the 19 August FOMC minutes. This is a general market-risk assessment for a public dashboard, not personalised financial advice, and no trade is being placed or recommended.
headline: Saturday morning of the CME weekend halt leaves NQ with no live price path anywhere in the 24-hour horizon: Tail holds low at 9% and EA_ON, while Stress is held at 45% because nothing resolved overnight - the strait stays shut under an active U.S. blockade, crude ended the week up about 5% at $82.40 WTI, and Friday's Retail Sales and Michigan sentiment both missed sharply.
body:
No live price path is available this hour. CME equity-index futures have been shut since Friday's 21:00 UTC weekly close and do not reopen until roughly 22:00 UTC on Sunday 16 August, so directional efficiency, pullback depth, repeated extension and proximity to session extremes are all unobservable for the entire current 24-hour horizon (05:00 UTC on 15 August to 04:00 UTC on 16 August). Everything below is the last confirmed state plus corroborated news, re-verified from primary sources this hour, and that limitation - not a judgement that markets are calm - is what caps Confidence below the solid band.

Last confirmed structure, re-verified this hour: NQ futures settled at 30,148.25, down 40.25 points or 0.13% from a 30,188.50 prior settlement, inside a 30,028.50-30,283.00 session band on 397,964 contracts, with the venue explicitly showing closed (Investing.com). The Nasdaq-100 cash index closed at 30,046.14, down 38.36 points or 0.13% against a 30,084.50 previous close, inside a 29,934.66-30,179.82 range and roughly 2.3% below its 52-week high of 30,762.20 (Yahoo Finance). Both the futures and the cash index therefore finished mid-range on a small down day with genuine two-way trade - not a persistent one-way liquidation, and not a close pinned to a session extreme. Nothing in that structure resembles the shallow-pullback, repeated-extension pattern required before Tail leaves the low band, which is why Tail stays at 9% rather than being lifted by the volatility backdrop alone.

Cross-asset: VIX closed at 14.25, down 2.60%, in a 14.18-14.72 day range and far below its 35.30 52-week high - equity volatility is not corroborating the geopolitical stress. The latest Federal Reserve H.15 shows the 2-year constant maturity at 4.15%, the 10-year at 4.63% and the 30-year at 5.21%; the curve is positively sloped and there is no yield shock aligned with the oil move. Crude remains the one aligned amplifier: WTI at $82.40, up 1.42% on the day and about 5% on the week, with Brent at $88.52, up 1.67%, monthly gains of 3.5% and 4.2% respectively and a yearly gain above 30% - crude snapped a two-week losing streak on the Hormuz impasse while the IEA warned of a deepening supply deficit (Trading Economics). An oil-only amplifier with VIX at 14 and yields quiet is a Stress input, not a Tail input; that conflict is precisely why Stress sits well above Tail.

Geopolitics, the dominant live thread and the reason Stress does not decay: the Strait of Hormuz remains effectively shut, with fewer than ten vessels a day transiting recently and the U.S. blockade having redirected dozens of ships since mid-July. Iran and Oman have agreed route coordinates - inbound lanes closer to Iran under Iranian oversight, outbound closer to Oman, no tolls - but Tehran's stated position is unchanged: as long as the U.S. naval blockade continues, the conditions for reopening do not exist, and full reopening is conditioned on U.S. concessions. Washington has answered with an indefinite-blockade posture, with the Treasury Secretary stating the blockade will keep anything from moving in or out of Iranian ports and the administration telling Americans to expect high fuel prices. Nothing new escalated or de-escalated in the hours since the previous run; this is an unresolved second information wave carried into Sunday's reopen, not a spent one.

Macro: Friday's U.S. data was notably soft on the consumer. July Retail Sales printed -0.6% month-on-month against a +0.1% consensus, the control group -0.4% against +0.3%, and ex-autos -0.3% against +0.2%; preliminary August Michigan Consumer Sentiment came in at 51.0 against 54.5 expected, with one-year inflation expectations ticking up to 4.3%. That is a second, independent risk channel unrelated to the Gulf, and it will interact with the FOMC minutes on 19 August - the only high-impact scheduled U.S. event in the next seven days, and roughly four days beyond this horizon. Nothing at all is scheduled inside the current 24 hours.

Synthesis: Tail 9% (low) states that pathological one-way price-path risk cannot be observed, and cannot form, while no venue is quoting; the non-zero floor prices the discontinuity a two-day headline gap carries into Sunday's open. Stress 45% (elevated) reflects a real and unresolved volatility backdrop - shut strait, active blockade standoff, crude up 5% on the week, soft consumer data - none of which a market holiday neutralises, and it is deliberately held rather than decayed because none of those threads resolved overnight. Confidence 59% (medium-low) is set by evidence quality: levels, volatility, yields, crude, catalysts and the seven-day calendar are all fresh and primary-sourced this hour, but the single most important input, the price path, is missing entirely and only Sunday's reopen restores it. Dominant mode is mixed. Jackson Hole (27-29 August) and Nvidia earnings (26 August) sit outside the seven-day window and are noted only as context.

lookbackSummary: Across the trailing 24 clock-hours Tail never left the low band, running 2-10% throughout. It held 9-10% through Friday's Asian and European sessions, eased to 7-9% across the U.S. cash session as the sharp Retail Sales and Michigan sentiment misses produced two-way volatility and rotation rather than directional efficiency, and printed 6% into the 21:00 UTC weekly close. Stress described a clear event arc: roughly 25-29% in the quiet pre-dawn hours, building to 40-44% through the U.S. cash session as the data landed, then 34% at the close. The two runs immediately after the close scored the halt itself at Tail 2% and Stress 12%; from 00:00 UTC onward that reading was corrected back to Tail 9% and Stress 45% on the judgement that a shut venue does not neutralise a live Hormuz closure, and 45% has now held for six consecutive hours including this one. Those past opinions are preserved exactly as published. Confidence spent the Friday session in the 30s-50s and has firmed to 56-59% since midnight as primary-source verification improved. One slot, 20:00 UTC on 14 August, has no published Claude assessment and is marked unavailable.
outlookSummary: The entire 24-hour horizon falls inside the CME weekend halt - it runs from 05:00 UTC on Saturday 15 August to 04:00 UTC on Sunday 16 August, ending roughly 18 hours before the reopen near 22:00 UTC that day - so neither a scheduled U.S. macro release nor a tradable price path falls within it. Tail is therefore projected flat at 9% for the first fifteen slots and ticking to 10% from 20:00 UTC on 15 August as the reopen edges into view; that increment reflects accumulating gap risk, not observed structure, and every slot stays in the low band, so the action is EA_ON and the status green throughout. Stress is projected to ease at most a point to 44% through the thin Saturday Gulf, Asian and European hours, when weekend headline flow is historically lightest, then firm back to 45-47% into the late slots as unresolved threads converge on Sunday's price discovery: the Hormuz impasse and Tehran's insistence that the blockade end first, the U.S. indefinite-blockade posture, the not-yet-signed Iran-Oman routing arrangement, and a soft U.S. consumer picture heading into the 19 August FOMC minutes. Confidence stays in the medium-low band at 58-59% for as long as no venue quotes. The real checkpoint sits just beyond this horizon: the reopen at roughly 22:00 UTC on 16 August, which the danger window brackets together with its first 90 minutes of trade. Gap risk there is two-way, and the first live tape - not this forecast - is what will decide whether Tail leaves the low band.
